rules.title: NSX Manager version is not exposed to known security advisories
rules.rationale: NSX Manager controls network and security policy for every workload.

mitigation.summary: Upgrade NSX to the fixed version.

rules.title: NSX release is within vendor general support
rules.rationale: Unsupported releases no longer receive routine security fixes.

mitigation.summary: Upgrade NSX to a supported release.

rules.title: NSX management cluster is stable
rules.rationale: A degraded management cluster risks policy realization failures and loss of quorum.

mitigation.summary: Restore all three manager nodes to a stable state.

rules.title: Scheduled NSX backups are configured
rules.rationale: Without backups, loss of the manager cluster means rebuilding all network and security policy.

mitigation.summary: Configure scheduled backups to an SFTP server outside the NSX domain; test restores.

rules.title: NSX Manager forwards logs to remote syslog
rules.rationale: Remote logs preserve evidence of administrative and firewall activity.

mitigation.summary: Configure syslog exporters (TLS where possible) on all manager nodes.
steps: System > Fabric > Profiles > Node Profiles > Syslog Servers

rules.title: NSX Manager time synchronization is configured
rules.rationale: Accurate time is required for log correlation and certificates.

mitigation.summary: Configure NTP servers in the node profile.

rules.title: API authentication lockout after 5 or fewer failures
rules.rationale: Limits password guessing against the NSX API.

mitigation.summary: Set api_max_auth_failures to 5 or less.

rules.title: API lockout period is at least 15 minutes
rules.rationale: Short lockout periods do not slow guessing.

mitigation.summary: Set api_failed_auth_lockout_period to 900 or more.

rules.title: Local password minimum length is sufficient
rules.rationale: Short local passwords are practical to brute force.

mitigation.summary: Increase minimum_password_length.

rules.title: NSX certificates are not expired or near expiry
rules.rationale: Expired certificates break management-plane trust and compute manager connectivity.

mitigation.summary: Replace expiring certificates.

rules.title: All transport nodes are realized successfully
rules.rationale: Hosts that failed realization may not enforce distributed firewall policy.

mitigation.summary: Resolve transport node realization errors.

rules.title: Distributed firewall is enabled
rules.rationale: With DFW disabled no east-west policy is enforced regardless of configured rules.

mitigation.summary: Enable the distributed firewall after validating policy.

rules.title: Default layer-3 DFW rule drops or rejects
rules.rationale: A default ALLOW makes every workload reachable unless an earlier rule denies it (no zero trust).

mitigation.summary: Move to default DROP after building allow rules from observed flows.
steps: Change default rule action to DROP

rules.title: Default layer-3 DFW rule logs traffic
rules.rationale: Logging the default rule reveals unexpected flows and supports policy tuning.

mitigation.summary: Enable logging on the default rule.
steps: Security > Distributed Firewall > Default rule > Logging

rules.title: DFW exclusion list contains no user workloads
rules.rationale: Excluded VMs are not protected by any distributed firewall rule.

mitigation.summary: Remove workloads from the exclusion list; use allow rules instead.
steps: Security > Distributed Firewall > Actions > Exclusion List

rules.title: No enabled any-any-any ALLOW rules
rules.rationale: An any-any-any allow negates segmentation for everything it applies to.

mitigation.summary: Replace with specific source, destination and service rules.

rules.title: Broad ALLOW rules restrict services
rules.rationale: ANY source or destination combined with ANY service grants excessive reachability.

mitigation.summary: Restrict services to those required.

rules.title: ALLOW rules scope Applied-To
rules.rationale: DFW-wide Applied-To pushes rules everywhere, widening unintended matches and consuming rule tables.

mitigation.summary: Set Applied-To to the groups the rule protects.

rules.title: Rules reference groups with effective members
rules.rationale: Configured policy is insufficient; groups without realized members make rules ineffective (Broadcom KB 414765).

mitigation.summary: Fix group criteria/tags or remove obsolete rules.

rules.title: Rules are not shadowed by earlier rules
rules.rationale: Shadowed rules never match, hiding intended denies or allows and complicating reviews.

mitigation.summary: Reorder, merge or delete shadowed rules.
steps: Review rule order within the category

rules.limitations: Configuration-inferred; context profiles, negation and dynamic identity rules are sent to manual review.

rules.title: No stale disabled rules
rules.rationale: Disabled rules accumulate and can be re-enabled accidentally.

mitigation.summary: Delete disabled rules that are no longer needed.

rules.title: Deny rules log matched traffic
rules.rationale: Logged denies provide detection of lateral movement attempts.

mitigation.summary: Enable logging on DROP/REJECT rules.

rules.title: Workload is covered by distributed firewall policy
rules.rationale: Workloads outside all policy groups fall through to the default rule.

mitigation.summary: Tag or group the workload and add explicit policy.

rules.limitations: Configuration-inferred from realized group membership; does not observe traffic.

rules.title: Gateway firewall default rules deny
rules.rationale: A default ALLOW on Tier-0 exposes internal segments to north-south traffic.

mitigation.summary: Set gateway default action to DROP after adding required allows.

rules.title: NAT rules do not bypass the gateway firewall
rules.rationale: firewall_match BYPASS lets translated traffic skip gateway firewall inspection.

mitigation.summary: Set NAT firewall match to MATCH_EXTERNAL_ADDRESS or MATCH_INTERNAL_ADDRESS.

rules.title: Distributed IDS/IPS is enabled where licensed
rules.rationale: IDS/IPS adds detection of exploitation attempts between workloads.

mitigation.summary: Enable distributed IDS/IPS on relevant clusters (licensing permitting).

rules.title: Federation / multi-tenancy context reviewed

check.guidance: If Federation, projects or VPCs are used, assess the Global Manager and each project scope separately

rules.rationale: Global and project-scoped policy is not visible from a single Local Manager default domain.

mitigation.summary: Add Global Manager / project scopes to the assessment.
